note.specFocus: Martin Luther King Jr as a worked example of a significant Christian figure whose faith shaped social action.
note.sourcePages: Written to match the Edexcel specification; no supplied booklet for this subject.
note.summary:
1.4 One Other Significant Christian — Martin Luther King Jr
Martin Luther King Jr (1929–1968) was a Baptist minister and the most prominent leader of the American Civil Rights Movement, whose Christian faith directly shaped his activism.
Key actions
• He led the Montgomery Bus Boycott (1955–56), a non-violent protest against racial segregation on public buses, sparked by Rosa Parks' arrest.
• He led the March on Washington (1963), delivering his famous "I Have a Dream" speech, drawing on biblical imagery of justice and equality.
• He wrote the "Letter from Birmingham Jail" (1963), defending non-violent civil disobedience using Christian moral reasoning.
• He was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize (1964) for his leadership, and was assassinated in 1968.
Why he is significant for Christians
• His commitment to non-violence was rooted in Jesus' teaching to "turn the other cheek" (Matthew 5:39) and to love one's enemies.
• His campaign for racial justice is seen by many as working for the "Kingdom of God" on earth, applying belief in imago Dei (that all people are made equally in God's image) to a major social injustice.
• His willingness to suffer and ultimately die for his beliefs is often compared to Christian ideas of sacrificial discipleship.
Exam link: be ready to compare King with other possible significant Christians (e.g. Mother Teresa, Pope John Paul II) when asked to discuss "the most significant Christian".

questions.examTip: Make two separate points and develop each one. Link the development directly to the question.
questions.modelAnswer:
A strong response develops two separate points:

1. As a Baptist minister, Martin Luther King Jr led the Civil Rights Movement in the United States using non-violent protest, including the Montgomery Bus Boycott (1955–56), grounding his campaign explicitly in Christian teaching about love, justice and human dignity.

2. In his "I Have a Dream" speech (1963) and his leadership of the March on Washington, King drew on biblical imagery, such as the prophets' call for justice, to argue that racial equality was a moral and religious obligation, not just a political goal.
questions.question: Outline two actions of Martin Luther King Jr which show his significance to Christians.

questions.examTip: For 6 marks, combine accurate knowledge with explanation. Explain why each point matters and link it directly to the question; avoid simply listing facts.
questions.modelAnswer:
A developed answer could explain the issue through three connected points.

First, King based his commitment to non-violent resistance on Jesus' teaching to "turn the other cheek" (Matthew 5:39) and on the example of love for enemies, showing Christians a model of how faith can directly inspire social and political action.

Second, His work in the Civil Rights Movement is seen by many Christians as an example of working for the Kingdom of God on earth, applying biblical teaching about justice, equality and the worth of every person made in the image of God to a real, urgent social problem.

Finally, King's willingness to suffer, be imprisoned and eventually be assassinated (1968) for his beliefs is often compared by Christians to the self-sacrifice of Jesus, making him an enduring example of costly Christian discipleship and moral courage.
questions.question: Explain why Martin Luther King Jr is a significant figure for Christians.

questions.examTip: For a 10-mark discussion, analyse different aspects of the Christian issue and how they interrelate. Finish with a reasoned conclusion; do not just list advantages and disadvantages.
questions.modelAnswer:
A FIRST PERSPECTIVE

One line of reasoning is: King's leadership of the Civil Rights Movement had a lasting impact on law and society in the United States, and his explicitly Christian, non-violent approach to justice continues to inspire campaigners and churches worldwide.

A second consideration is: His writings and speeches, grounded in scripture, show how Christian faith can be applied to major social issues, making him a powerful example of practical discipleship rather than only private belief.

AN ALTERNATIVE PERSPECTIVE

A different perspective is: Other twentieth-century Christians could be argued as equally or more significant in different ways, for example Mother Teresa's decades of direct care for the poorest in Calcutta, or Pope John Paul II's influence on global Catholicism and his role in the fall of communism in Eastern Europe.

A further consideration is: Significance can be measured differently: King is especially significant for linking Christian faith to political and social justice, while others are significant chiefly through acts of personal charity or through leadership of the wider Church.

JUDGEMENT

Overall, the conclusion should weigh the arguments above against this key consideration: judging who is "most" significant depends on whether significance is measured by social and political impact, by direct charitable service, or by influence on the institutional Church, and different Christians would reasonably disagree. It should then state which perspective is more convincing in relation to the exact wording of the question and explain why, rather than assuming that every Christian will reach the same view.
questions.question: Discuss whether Martin Luther King Jr is the most significant Christian of the twentieth century.

questions.examTip: Use accurate Christian teaching, explain why each point matters, and in an evaluation compare arguments before reaching a reasoned conclusion.
questions.modelAnswer:
A FIRST PERSPECTIVE
Teaching gives coherent meaning to the themes of Christian equality, agape, non-violence, social justice and civil rights and helps Christians decide what is true.

AN ALTERNATIVE PERSPECTIVE
Practice makes belief visible in worship, compassion, family and service; without action faith may be empty. Christians within different traditions may also disagree about how the teaching should be lived.

JUDGEMENT
A reasoned conclusion should compare the authority and practical effect of belief and action, acknowledge diversity, and decide which is more persuasive for the exact claim.

Evaluate this statement, referring to Christianity.
